author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A sustained increase in energy prices could begin to weigh on household consumption in the euro zone by autumn, European Central Bank Chief Economist Philip Lane said Friday. Speaking at a conference in Ireland, Lane emphasized that the effect depends on whether the current rise persists.

The warning puts household demand at the center of the energy shock facing Europe. Higher power and fuel bills can leave consumers with less money for other purchases, while also complicating the inflation outlook that guides interest-rate decisions. Lane did not announce a policy change or provide a new forecast, describing the issue instead as a continuing source of uncertainty.

For markets, the comment highlights the two-sided challenge confronting the ECB: energy costs can lift inflation even as they weaken growth by reducing spending. Investors will therefore be watching incoming consumption and price data for evidence of which effect is becoming stronger. Lane’s remarks were made before new autumn data are available, so they are a risk assessment rather than a conclusion that demand has already declined.
dek: The central bank’s chief economist said the duration of higher energy costs remains an important uncertainty for euro-zone households and policymakers.
headline: ECB’s Lane says persistent energy rise could hit autumn consumption
